style: carry on from the previous verse in one line

candidates.angle: rajas leads to birth among those attached to action
candidates.evidence: रजसि प्रलयं गत्वा कर्मसङ्गिषु जायते (having gone to dissolution in rajas is born among those attached to action)

candidates.angle: tamas leads to birth among deluded forms
candidates.evidence: तथा प्रलीनस्तमसि मूढयोनिषु जायते (similarly having dissolved in tamas is born among deluded births)

candidates.angle: the state of mind at death shapes the next birth

en.intro: Krishna finishes the picture of the gunas by looking at the two lower paths. Listen to how the state of mind at death shapes the next birth.
en.notice: One word reveals the fate of restless desire, rajas. A being who dies in rajas is born among those attached to action, caught again in the very cycle of work that binds them.
en.next: Krishna now explains that the result of rajasic action is suffering, while the result of tamasic action is ignorance and delusion.
en.meaning: A being who dies in rajas is born among those attached to action. A being who dies in tamas is born among deluded forms.

hi.intro: कृष्ण गीता के इस अध्याय में गुणों के दो निचले रास्तों को पूरा करते हैं। सुनिए, मृत्यु के समय मन की स्थिति अगले जन्म को कैसे तय करती है।
hi.meaning: रजोगुण के बढ़ने पर मरने वाला प्राणी मनुष्य योनि में जन्म लेता है तथा तमोगुण के बढ़ने पर मरने वाला मूढ़ योनि में जन्म लेता है ॥
hi.notice: एक शब्द, रजसि, बेचैन इच्छा की नियति बताता है। जो प्राणी रजोगुण में मरता है, वह कर्मसङ्गि में जन्म लेता है, यानी फिर से उसी कर्म के बंधन में फँस जाता है।
hi.next: कृष्ण अब बताते हैं कि रजोगुण के कर्म का फल दुख है, तथा तमोगुण के कर्म का फल अज्ञान और मोह है।
